clue.text: Enters a pet prepared for showing — gets through

indicators.note: letters made ready for display are worked into a new order here

explanation.surface: Someone enters their pet in a show and gets through the judging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared for showing' rearranges ENTERS A PET; the dash then leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate is to pierce or pass into and through something.

clue.text: The guy going round in circles?

definitions.text: The guy going round in circles?

parts.words: The guy going round in circles?
parts.note: a man's first name that is also a swirling current of water

explanation.surface: A fellow who keeps going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling current turns in circles, and the same word is a boy's name.

clue.text: Sets up secret organisation

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of secret are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a clandestine organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to build or set something upright.

clue.text: Said to be penned below or round building

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: penned means wrote and below means under

explanation.surface: A building said to be written beneath or round something.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building, often domed.

clue.text: Rested up before week-end work

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rested means sat
the end of the word week is K

explanation.surface: Resting before the weekend's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done.

clue.text: Went wrong, yet remained about right!

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: remained means stayed

explanation.surface: Went astray, yet stayed in the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander off course or into error.

clue.text: The medico increased the head's gloom

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
increased means rose
a ness is a headland, a head of land

explanation.surface: The doctor made the headmaster's gloom worse.
explanation.walkthrough: A NESS is a headland, seen in Scottish place names like Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Moroseness is sullen gloominess, a sulky ill humour.

clue.text: Feeling nothing I sent in 10 to be massacred

indicators.note: massacred means the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: 10 is ten

explanation.surface: Feeling nothing as ten are sent in to be slaughtered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insentient means lacking feeling or consciousness.

clue.text: A boy carries nothing in time

indicators.note: the boy holds the next piece within himself, as one carries a load

parts.note: a boy is a son
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lad is carrying nothing, but will be on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming soon arrives before long, in a short while.

clue.text: An individual never short of puff.

definitions.text: An individual never short of puff.

parts.words: An individual never short of puff.
parts.note: puff here is promotional hype rather than breath: someone always talking up a product

explanation.surface: A person who is never out of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Puff is exaggerated praise used to promote, the stock in trade of one who promotes goods in the media.

clue.text: A means of support on the beach…

parts.note: a shore is a prop or beam that holds up a wall

explanation.surface: A support found on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land beside the sea, having come off the water, is being on the beach.

clue.text: … can cause disease

indicators.note: the word disease can give rise to a new arrangement of its own letters

explanation.surface: Continuing from the beach: a day by the sea can make you ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 11 across, whose beach gives the sense; 'can cause' signals that DISEASE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast, a resort or the shore is where polluted bathing water might make visitors ill.

clue.text: They'll supply a demand for some as-new contrivance when money's involved

indicators.note: involved means the money is wrapped inside the rearranged letters
a contrivance is a device made up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L stands for pounds, money

explanation.surface: Some as-new goods are on offer where cash changes hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrivance' rearranges SOME AS-NEW, and 'involved' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sales staff meet customers' demand by selling them goods.

clue.text: It's not beneath the directors to be honest!

parts.note: not beneath means above
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Directors are above being dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something above board is open and legitimate, with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Show about fifty in to dine

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the word for dining

parts.note: to dine is to eat
C is circa, about
L is Roman fifty

explanation.surface: A show for about fifty diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is showy brilliance or ostentatious display.

clue.text: Most profound river-side irritant

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a pest is an annoying nuisance

explanation.surface: The most serious nuisance on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' is just a link joining river to irritant; the Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound and deep both describe great depth of thought or feeling, here in the superlative.

clue.text: Fed-up and upset serving men causing delay

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word fed from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: upset turns the serving men upside down, backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, men serving in the army

explanation.surface: Fed up and upset servicemen cause delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to postpone or put off.

clue.text: Bill and Edward took part

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Two men, Bill and Edward, joined in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to play a part in a performance.

clue.text: The diver made to look a fool

definitions.meaning: a diving waterbird of northern lakes

explanation.surface: A diving bird made to look silly.
explanation.definitionFit: The diving bird and a silly, crazy person share the same short name.

clue.text: Hand over the church keys

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
D and E are musical keys

explanation.surface: Giving the church its keys back.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or give up something to another.

clue.text: Paid pounds for a mallet

parts.note: paid means gave, as in gave money
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone paid good money for a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer's or judge's small hammer is a type of mallet.

clue.text: More tender grub is set before the monarch

indicators.note: set before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: a gentle is a maggot, an angler's grub
R is rex or regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: Food served to the king first is more tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food; it is a maggot, which anglers call a gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentler means kinder, more mild or soft.

clue.text: Extracts from French article about all and sundry

indicators.note: about means the French article goes around the other word

parts.note: les is a French definite article
all and sundry means each one

explanation.surface: Excerpts from a French piece about everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: To leach is to draw out a substance by percolating liquid through.

clue.text: The company filled up with a simple fruit-juice drink

indicators.note: the company is stuffed full with the next piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: a set is a group of people, a company
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb

explanation.surface: A firm topped up with a plain fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like an adjective for the drink but is the noun for a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a cooling Middle Eastern drink of diluted fruit juice, now also a frozen dessert.

clue.text: New rope-it's to be put away

indicators.note: new means the letters of rope-it's are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new rope must be stored.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposit is to store or deposit something for safekeeping.

clue.text: He'll start, being in love, to pen erotic verses

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: verses contain some lines, so these words hold letters within

explanation.surface: Being in love, he begins to write erotic poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener starts things off, like a batsman in cricket.

clue.text: A musician, one appearing in kinky boots

indicators.note: the numeral shows up inside the twisted boots
kinky means twisted, so the letters of boots are bent into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A performer turns up wearing kinky boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' rearranges BOOTS to OBOST, and 'appearing in' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the oboe is a woodwind musician.

clue.text: A Mercian king of note

parts.note: taken as written
fa is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A notable king of Mercia.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of central England; Offa built Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the eighth century.

clue.text: Water, pure and simple

explanation.surface: Water, nothing more nor less.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lake is a body of water; also the adjective meaning nothing more than.

clue.text: He doesn't go about things in the right way

definitions.text: He doesn't go about things in the right way

parts.words: He doesn't go about things in the right way
parts.note: seems to describe someone who behaves badly, but means one who uses the other hand

explanation.surface: Disapproval of someone who does things wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone favouring the left hand rather than the right does tasks the other way round.

clue.text: Some people swear never to accept pay for work

indicators.note: some of these words holds the answer within them

explanation.surface: Some folk vow never to take wages for labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive money in return for labour.

clue.text: Taken in yet again!

parts.note: seems to describe someone conned once more, but means soaked up a second time

explanation.surface: Fooled once more!
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbing means soaking up, and doing it a second time is soaking it up once more.
